title: One vault format at version 1: drop the state-document compatibility surface (DEC-38 A)
description:
DEC-38, accepted 2026-09-29, option A, read from opum-agent tracker where it is recorded (the orchestrator relay is what asked for the work; the record is what was read). It resolves ODOC-OP-2026-09-29-06 item 1, the operator direction that before the first release the on-disk format is simply the format and not a compatibility contract, because nobody and no repository is using Ward and the only vault in existence is the operator own test vault holding one valueless test value.

WHY THE VERSION GATE COMES OUT: the version gate is not what protects anything. Measured on dev at 53100a3: test/project-documents.test.ts:680 already asserts that a genuine format-1 document, eight-key audit record and all, is refused for its RECORD shape as vault_state_malformed by the strict key-set reader when only its version number is changed. The reader refuses those bytes either way. The version added a name, not a protection.

WHAT IS DROPPED: the state document version-mismatch branch in parseVaultState, the doctor state_unsupported code, the StateObservation unsupported variant, the retained verbatim format-1 fixture in test/project-documents.test.ts with its two tests, the four command-path refusal tests plus the doctor case and the rewritten-as-format-2 control in test/vault-format-refusal.test.ts, and the case at test/reporting.test.ts:530. Floor of about 20 lines of src and 190 of test.

WHAT IS KEPT: vault_format_unsupported at exactly two sites, the sealed envelope header in src/domain/envelope.ts:92 and a stored profile approval whose snapshotVersion differs in src/domain/vault-state.ts:363. Neither is the state-document format. The envelope version is bound as GCM authenticated data and is genuinely the outer container format; the snapshot version guards against re-reading an approval under different normalization, which is an authority question. DEC-26 no-hint and DEC-30 sentence survive unchanged at both. The strict key-set reader is kept: it is the actual refusal in every case.

CONSTRAINTS: stay out of ~/.ward and the keychain entirely; the operator re-creates the test vault on their own machine. Ward must keep working with neither Lore nor Quest installed.

DEFERRED AND RECORDED AS DEFERRED: the next field added to an audit record before release breaks reads in both directions again, because the reader compares key sets exactly. That recurrence question is DEC-38 option C, explicitly left for the first release rather than answered here.

acceptanceCriteria.text: vaultStateFormatVersion is 1 and every path that writes the state document writes that value
parseVaultState answers a formatVersion that is not this build with vault_state_malformed

The state-document version-mismatch branch is deleted and no path raises vault_format_unsupported for the state document own version, while the reporting path keeps its answer for the retained approval site instead of throwing
vault_format_unsupported is still raised by the sealed envelope header and by a stored profile approval whose snapshotVersion differs, each keeping the DEC-30 sentence and the no-hint shape
The retained format-1 fixture and the four command-path refusal tests are deleted, and no test asserts the removed behaviour
ADR 0010 records one format at version 1 and names only the two remaining refusal sites

plan: Return vaultStateFormatVersion to 1 and make parseVaultState answer a wrong version with vault_state_malformed instead of vault_format_unsupported
Delete the StateObservation unsupported variant, the observeState catch for vault_format_unsupported and the doctor state_unsupported case in reporting.ts
Delete the retained format-1 fixture and its two tests in project-documents.test.ts, and update the reporting.test.ts expectation to state_malformed
Delete the four command-path refusal tests, the doctor case and the rewrite-as-format-2 control from vault-format-refusal.test.ts, keeping the two surviving sites asserted
Rewrite ADR 0010 to record one format at version 1 and only the two remaining refusal sites
Run bun run check green and have an independent reviewer verify the change against the DEC-38 record
implementationNotes:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW, 2026-09-29, found one real defect in the first draft and four documentation inaccuracies. All five are fixed in the same branch.

F1, the defect, and it is mine at the packet stage rather than the implementation stage. The first draft deleted the reporting path answer for vault_format_unsupported (the StateObservation unsupported variant, the observeState case and the doctor state_unsupported code) on the stated ground that it was unreachable once the state-document version gate went. That was false. parseVaultState still raises the same code for a stored profile approval whose snapshotVersion differs, so the code still reaches the reporting path from the approval site. Removing the handling made both reports throw out of their read: measured, ward doctor and ward status each exited 6 with EMPTY stdout, breaking ADR 0007 contract that doctor always reports all five checks and that the report reaches stdout either way, and making ward status exit a code its own manifest does not declare. Fixed by restoring the status, the observeState case and the doctor case, with comments saying what the status now means, and pinned by a new test in test/reporting.test.ts that was measured failing against the unfixed source (empty stdout, JSON parse error) before the fix went back in.

F2a: src/contract/errors.ts still said one code for three sites. Now two, with the third recorded as removed.
F2b: ADR 0010 claimed doctor answers state_malformed and that it is the only answer now. False for the approval site, which answers state_unsupported. Corrected, and the correction records that a first draft deleted it on a false unreachability assumption.
F2c: ADR 0010 claimed ward status never reads the state document. False, and it was carried over from the previous ADR where it was already wrong: status reads the state to produce its binding row, and exits 0 because bindingStatus maps a non-present state to unknown. Corrected.
F3: the snapshot-version test fixture used snapshot: {} with a comment claiming it was valid in every other respect; normalizeProfile refuses that value, so the record had a second reason to be refused. Replaced with a complete canonical snapshot, which makes the comment true and the isolation real.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DECISION RECORD: DEC-38 accepted outcome lists doctor state_unsupported among the things dropped. That line is now wrong and the code is right; the drop is only the state-document version branch, and the doctor case survives for the approval site. Routed to opum-agent so opum-doc and the DEC-38 record can be corrected rather than left describing code that does not exist.

WHAT THE REVIEW CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY, which is the part worth keeping: the positive control in the rewritten vault-format-refusal test is real, measured by running the rewritten file unchanged against a git archive of dev, where it is 2 pass and 1 fail, the failing case being exactly the new control. So that file does not pass against the old source and would fail again if the third site were restored. The reviewer also enumerated every occurrence of the code in src and found no unintended third raiser, and confirmed the store format_version column is the envelope version and untouched.
finalSummary:
DEC-38 option A implemented and promoted. The vault state document is back to version 1, its version is an ordinary field validated like every other, and vault_format_unsupported survives at exactly the two sites that are not this format: the sealed envelope header, bound as authenticated data, and a stored profile approval snapshotVersion, which guards an authority question. DEC-26 no-hint rule and DEC-30 sentence are unchanged at both.

Landed as opum-ai/ward-cli#99 (squash 61aa8a2), then promoted to main by fast-forwarding origin/dev into it and reading origin/main back by ref: main and dev are both 61aa8a24d6818fcdc852bddfb5267252e83f4161, and main was empty of rules when measured, so no check was configured there and none was waited on. All six required checks were green on the promoted SHA.

HOW IT WAS VERIFIED. bun run check green at 646 tests and 0 fail. lore validate --strict, lore check --strict, lore agents --check and the lore agent-source-coverage script all exit 0. An independent reviewer confirmed by measurement, not by reading: it ran the rewritten vault-format-refusal test file unchanged against a git archive of dev and got 2 pass and 1 fail, the failing case being exactly the new positive control, so that file does not pass against the old source and would fail again if the third site were restored. It also enumerated every raiser of the code in src and confirmed no unintended third one.

WHAT REVIEW CHANGED, and the reason AC3 is not the criterion that was filed. The first commit deleted the reporting path answer for vault_format_unsupported on a claim of unreachability that was false — the claim was mine, written into the decision packet, and acceptance turned it into an instruction. parseVaultState still raises that code for a stored approval snapshotVersion, so the code still reaches the reporting path. Measured effect of the deletion: ward doctor and ward status each exited 6 with EMPTY stdout, breaking ADR 0007 contract that doctor always reports all five checks and that the report reaches stdout either way, and making ward status exit a code its own manifest does not declare. Fixed by restoring the status, the observeState case and the doctor case, and pinned by a test measured failing against the unfixed source before the fix went back in.

AC3 was amended rather than checked as filed. It read that the StateObservation unsupported variant and the doctor state_unsupported case are deleted and no path can produce them. That is now false and the code is right, so checking it would have been a checked box over a disproved claim. It now reads what is true: the state-document version branch is gone, no path raises the code for the document own version, and the reporting path keeps its answer for the retained approval site instead of throwing.

Four documentation inaccuracies were also corrected: the error catalogue still counted three raising sites, ADR 0010 claimed doctor only answer was state_malformed, the same ADR claimed ward status never reads the state document (carried over from the previous ADR, where it was already wrong, since status does read it to produce its binding row), and a test fixture used an empty snapshot while its comment claimed the record was valid in every other respect.

CARRIED FORWARD RATHER THAN CLOSED. WCLI-52 was filed for the residual the review found untracked: runBackup seals a plaintext it never parses, so a state document that decrypts but does not parse still produces a backup restore will refuse. WCLI-53 was filed for a CI flake measured during the promotion, not just retried: test/key-provider.test.ts:293 asserts wall-clock elapsed under 400 ms, and it failed at 474 ms on one of two runs of the SAME SHA while the other passed, with the two runs overlapping by 26 seconds on the same runner group.
